title: Emrys and the Homecoming
premise: Xanthe Hartwell, seventeen, has spent four years keeping her head down at Hollow Creek High while raising her siblings and counting the days to graduation. When a college application essay asks her to write about an injustice she witnessed, the words she's buried pour out: the school board quietly expelled a homeless classmate, Emrys, to protect a star athlete and a funding deal. As Xanthe digs through buried records with help from an unlikely found family—a retired janitor, a burned-out teacher, and her own siblings—she risks her scholarship, her mother's job, and her carefully invisible life. In the end she publishes the truth the night before graduation, Emrys walks across the stage to receive his diploma, and Xanthe submits an essay that finally tells the whole story.
about_author: J. M. Ravensworth is the pen name of a former night-shift librarian who grew up in a mill town and never left, at least not on paper. They write young adult stories about kids who hold families together and the small, stubborn acts that count as justice.

chapters.title: The Question Nobody Can Stop Answering
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Between packing lunches, signing her brother's permission slip, and covering her sister's shift anxiety, Xanthe opens the college application and freezes at the essay prompt about injustice. She writes one sentence about a boy named Emrys, then deletes it. Emotional beat: the crack in her invisibility—curiosity she can't unfeel.

chapters.title: The Empty Desk
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. She notices Emrys's desk has been empty for weeks and no one will say why. A guidance clerk lets slip he was 'administratively withdrawn.' Flashback threads establish their brief friendship before he lost his housing. Emotional beat: guilt—the moment she realizes she looked away on purpose.

chapters.title: Night Shift, Night School
chapters.summary: Dual POV: Xanthe at home managing a feverish sibling while their mother works; short Emrys interlude at the library where he still studies, refusing to quit. Xanthe finds his old backpack in the lost-and-found, untouched for a month. Emotional beat: the ache of parallel lives and the first spark of resolve.

chapters.title: The Janitor Who Remembers Everything
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. She approaches Mr. Okonkwo, the retiring janitor who kept copies of maintenance logs showing the gym renovation tied to a donor's condition: 'no vagrants on campus.' He warns her what happened to the last kid who asked questions. Emotional beat: found family begins—an adult who finally sees her.

chapters.title: What the Board Buried
chapters.summary: Xanthe and Mr. Okonkwo piece together minutes from a closed session: the expulsion was engineered to satisfy the Hartwell family's donor—no relation, a cruel coincidence Xanthe must sit with. Her teacher Ms. Reyes hesitantly confirms she was told to stay silent. Emotional beat: outrage hardening into purpose, shadowed by her own name on the documents.

chapters.title: Detention of One
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Her digging gets noticed; she's threatened with losing the attendance-based scholarship she needs. Her mother, exhausted, begs her to stop—for once, not out of fear but because she can't lose anything else. Xanthe nearly burns the evidence. Emotional beat: the lowest point—justice priced in her family's survival.

chapters.title: The Sibling Summit
chapters.summary: POV shifts to her younger sister Priya, who found the hidden documents and has already made copies with her friends. The siblings confront Xanthe: they're not fragile, they're in. Even the youngest offers his savings for printing costs. Emotional beat: the turn—found family isn't just comfort; it's a crew.

chapters.title: Ninety-Six Hours
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Countdown structure: the board meets Friday, graduation is Saturday. The crew distributes copies, contacts a local reporter, and Emrys himself appears at her door—angry she's risking everything, then choosing to stand with her. Emotional beat: terror and solidarity braided together as the clock runs down.

chapters.title: Open Session
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. At the board meeting she reads the closed-session minutes aloud, name and all, as the gym fills with students, Ms. Reyes, and the reporter. The donor deal collapses; the superintendent resigns mid-meeting. Xanthe is escorted out—but the story is already everywhere. Emotional beat: the climax—cost fully paid, truth fully spoken.

chapters.title: Emrys and the Homecoming
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Graduation day: the board, cornered by the exposé, reinstates Emrys and grants his diploma. He crosses the stage to a standing ovation while Xanthe watches from the bleachers, unbothered by her own delayed clearance. She mails her essay—unedited, honest—to the college. Emotional beat: homecoming not to a place, but to a self no longer invisible.
